after:
An object can link to another object called its prototype.

If a property is missing from the object itself, JavaScript looks along that link. This lets an object use shared defaults.

`Object.create(defaults)` makes a new object linked to `defaults`.
```javascript
const defaults = { color: "teal" };
const badge = Object.create(defaults);
console.log(badge.color);
```
Output:
```text
teal
```
The badge has no color of its own, so the lookup finds the color on `defaults`.

An own property is stored directly on an object. An inherited property is found through its prototype.

JavaScript checks the object's own properties first.

A prototype link is not a copied snapshot.

If the object has no own property with that name, later changes to the default can show up when the property is read.
